acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Rust/Metal page-dialog action buttons, native theme/font/event/AX adapters and Rust linked/trailing row layout. Native page-dialog title/window/modal and domain authority remain.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: Page alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload action controls contain no MdTextButton or native/hidden Label in the opt-in backend. SceneTextButton reuses Rust RowPointer input and kind19 scene/CPU recipes; one action-group Metal canvas presents the row. Views mode keeps its original native buttons.

Rust dialog_actions_layout owns width linking up to the platform link limit, native-order trailing row placement, padding and narrow clipping. Native platform services supply font/control metrics, theme colors, row insets/spacing and OK-leading order. No new font or UI framework is introduced.

PageDialogClient replaces the private DialogClientView button allocator through its hierarchy adapter. The inherited empty row never owns native controls. It retains native ClientView content adoption, Escape, input-protection, window background and observer teardown. Native GetOkButton/GetCancelButton are null for this custom client; PageDialogs exposes an explicit button adapter for its tests. No engine source changed.

Native DialogDelegate retains button masks, labels/styles, enabled/default metadata, Accept/Cancel and synchronous window close. Only actual native platform defaults register Return on Rust action nodes and project default AX state; macOS beforeunload Cancel-default Return behavior stays unchanged. Initially focused prompt/default controls retain native focus services. Composition admission and generation/profile/frame authorization remain native.

Action callbacks reject hidden windows, apply the same native IsPossiblyUnintendedInteraction and ShouldIgnoreButtonPressedEventHandling checks, then call native AcceptDialog/CancelDialog. Existing callbacks keep renderer responses posted off the button stack. Native model updates rebuild the Rust row and restore matching enabled focused controls; destroyed row weak callbacks and default accelerators are released.

Two Rust tests cover linked/trailing geometry, the long-label link limit, empty/narrow rows and clipping. A shared browser case compares original native button/row preferred metrics for all four dialog roles, verifies order and AX/default/name/childless controls, actual Metal caption visibility, native-label/enable updates, a deterministically blocked input activation and actual Cocoa mouse/Space activation. Existing Cocoa Return/Escape, prompt IME, stale-navigation, beforeunload and CloseNow cases remain in the critical and full inventories.

No dependency, browser-service operation, normal app/profile, installed bundle or signing changed. Native page-dialog title/frame/modal container, other forms/service panels and native event/focus/AX/scroll/window ownership remain open. This is a button/row migration checkpoint, not complete Views removal or a controlled performance result.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Native page-dialog title/frame and modal containers, other forms/panels/layouts, remaining form construction/service wording and native event/focus/AX/scroll/window ownership remain open. Native browser validation, authority, stores and operations remain explicit adapters.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, global RTL, typography/scale/pixel fidelity, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
